blocks.title: Sample Problem 6.12
blocks.problem:
For the reaction:
CaSO₄(s) → Ca²⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq)
Calculate ΔH°, ΔS° and ΔG° at 25 °C using the following data; and discuss its spontaneity.
Heat of Formation: ΔH°f [CaSO₄(s)] = -1432.7 kJ, ΔH°f [Ca²⁺(aq)] = -543.0 kJ, ΔH°f [SO₄²⁻(aq)] = -907.5 kJ
Standard entropy: S°[CaSO₄(s)] = 106.7 J/K, S°[Ca²⁺(aq)] = –55.2 J/K, S°[SO₄²⁻(aq)] = +17.2 J/K
blocks.answer: Result: We conclude that this process is nonspontaneous at standard conditions at 25 °C

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: (–55.2 + 17.2) – 106.7 = –144.7 J/K, not –1447 J/K; the book itself continues with –0.1447 kJ/K, so ΔG° = +25.3 kJ is right.

blocks.title: Sample Problem 6.13
blocks.problem:
What is the standard free-energy, ΔG° for the following reaction (Haber’s process) at 25°C?
N₂(g) + 3 H₂(g) → 2 NH₃(g)
Also discuss its spontaneity.
Heat of Formation: ΔH°f [N₂(g)] = 0 kJ, ΔH°f [H₂(g)] = 0 kJ, ΔH°f [NH₃(g)] = –45.9 kJ
Standard entropy: S°[N₂(g)] = 191.5 J/K, S°[H₂(g)] = 130.6 J/K, S°[NH₃(g)] = +193 J/K
blocks.answer: Result: Since ΔG° is a negative value, thus it is concluded that Haber’s process is spontaneous at standard conditions , i.e. at 25 °C.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: ΔH° was found as –91.8 kJ, so the ΔG° line should use –91.8 kJ, not –91.88 kJ: ΔG° = –91.8 – 298 × (–0.197) = –33.1 kJ.
